title: Cultural Differences & Etiquette
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Entender las diferencias culturales y la etiqueta de negocios es fundamental para el éxito internacional.

stages.title: Etiqueta y Cultura en los Negocios

parts.visual:
Primeras impresiones: 
- Shake hands (Dar la mano). 
- Small talk (Conversación trivial/ligera para romper el hielo). 
- Dress code (Código de vestimenta). 
Ej: In the US, it is common to shake hands and make some small talk before a meeting.
parts.audio: First impressions. Shake hands. Small talk is light conversation about things like the weather or sports. Dress code means the rules for what clothes to wear. For example: In the US, it is common to shake hands and make some small talk before a meeting.

parts.visual:
Comportamiento: 
- Punctuality (Puntualidad). 
- Polite / Impolite (Educado / Maleducado). 
- Eye contact (Contacto visual). 
Ej: Punctuality is very important in Germany. Being late is considered impolite.
parts.audio: Behavior. Punctuality means being on time. Polite means having good manners. Impolite means having bad manners. Eye contact means looking directly at someone's eyes. For example: Punctuality is very important in Germany. Being late is considered impolite.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige la palabra correcta de etiqueta y cultura.

questions.question: Before discussing the contract, we made some ____ talk about the weather. (Conversación ligera).
questions.explanation: Small talk = conversación trivial o ligera para romper el hielo.

questions.question: In Western business culture, it's normal to ____ hands when you meet someone. (Dar la mano).
The company has a strict dress ____. You must wear a suit. (Código).
____ is very important in Japan. You must never be late. (Puntualidad).
It is considered ____ to check your phone during a meeting. (Maleducado / Descortés).
questions.explanation: Impolite = maleducado, de mala educación (también se dice 'rude').

questions.question: Please be ____ to the clients, even if they are angry. (Educado / Cortés).
Maintaining eye ____ shows confidence in an interview. (Contacto visual).
In some Asian cultures, it is respectful to ____ instead of shaking hands. (Hacer una reverencia).
At the end of the presentation, please hand out your business ____. (Tarjetas de presentación).
Interrupting someone while they are speaking is very ____. (Grosero).
In international business, it's important to respect cultural ____. (Diferencias).
Our office is very ____. You can wear jeans and a t-shirt. (Informal / Relajado).
questions.explanation: Casual = informal (aplicado a la vestimenta o ambiente).

questions.question: A ____ environment means you have to wear a suit and tie. (Formal).
In many countries, you should address your boss by their ____ name, not their first name. (Apellido).
You should use a respectful ____ when writing to the CEO. (Tono).
A firm ____ shows confidence when you meet someone. (Apretón de manos).
Please observe proper table ____ during the business dinner. (Modales / Etiqueta).
questions.explanation: Manners = modales (table manners = modales en la mesa).

questions.question: It is customary to bring a small ____ when invited to someone's home. (Regalo).
Pointing with your finger is considered a bad ____ in some cultures. (Gesto).
Understanding business ____ is key to closing deals abroad. (Etiqueta).
questions.explanation: Etiquette = etiqueta (las reglas de comportamiento correcto).

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe la palabra correcta de etiqueta y cultura.

questions.question: To ____ hands. (Dar la mano con S)
____ talk. (Conversación trivial con S)
Dress ____. (Código de vestimenta con C)
Eye ____. (Contacto visual con C)
Being late is ____. (Maleducado/Descortés con I)
Please be ____. (Educado con P)
Business ____. (Tarjetas con C plural)
Interrupting is ____. (Grosero con R)
Table ____. (Modales con M)
Business ____. (Etiqueta con E)
